## Overview

`cellucid_prepare()` writes single-cell data -- embeddings, cell and gene
metadata, gene expression, a neighbour graph, and vector fields -- as a
**Cellucid-ready AnnData**: a standard AnnData store, written as AnnData Zarr,
that Python's anndata reads like any other and the Cellucid web app opens
directly. Gene expression is stored gene-major, so the viewer reads one gene
with one small range of the file, and `uns['cellucid']` carries the dataset's
name, citation, source, and launch defaults.

`format` chooses the output, and has no default because only you know where
the store goes: `format = "zarr"` writes a `.zarr` folder of small files, the
way to publish on GitHub (no file over 100 MB, no LFS); `format = "zarr.zip"`
writes the same store as one `.zarr.zip` file. `out_path` ends in the matching
suffix. (An `.h5ad` file is written by Python's
`cellucid.prepare(format = "h5ad")`; this package writes no HDF5, so it needs no
HDF5 library.)

## Minimal example

```{r}
library(cellucid)

umap <- matrix(c(0, 0,
                 1, 0,
                 0, 1,
                 1, 1),
               ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)
pca <- matrix(c(0, 3, 1,
                2, 5, 1,
                4, 0, 2,
                1, 1, 1),
              ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)

obs <- data.frame(
  cluster = factor(c("A", "A", "B", "B")),
  score = c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4),
  row.names = paste0("cell", 1:4)
)

expr <- matrix(c(0, 1,
                 2, 3,
                 4, 5,
                 0, 0),
               nrow = 4, byrow = TRUE,
               dimnames = list(rownames(obs), c("ENSG01", "ENSG02")))

var <- data.frame(symbol = c("CD3E", "MS4A1"), row.names = colnames(expr))

store <- cellucid_prepare(
  out_path = file.path(tempdir(), "vignette.zarr"),
  format = "zarr",
  embeddings = list(X_umap = umap, X_pca = pca),
  dataset_id = "vignette",
  dataset_name = "Vignette dataset",
  obs = obs,
  var = var,
  gene_expression = expr,
  embedding_defaults = c("2d" = "X_umap"),
  latent_key = "X_pca",
  var_gene_id_column = "symbol",
  force = TRUE
)

list.files(store, all.files = TRUE, no.. = TRUE)
```

In the web app at <https://www.cellucid.com>, open a `.zarr.zip` file from your
computer (see below), or a `.zarr` folder or `.zarr.zip` file published at a web
address with the **Link or server** address bar. In Python:

```python
import anndata
adata = anndata.read_zarr("vignette.zarr")
```

## What goes where

| Argument | In the store |
| --- | --- |
| `embeddings` | `obsm[<key>]`, float32, every column |
| `obs` | `obs`, every column |
| `var` | `var`, every column |
| `gene_expression` | `X`, gene-major float32 (`csc_matrix` for a sparse matrix) |
| `connectivities` | `obsp['connectivities']`, float32 `csr_matrix` |
| `vector_fields` | `obsm['<field>_<basis>']` for the embedding `X_<basis>` |
| `dataset_id`, `dataset_name`, `dataset_description` | `uns['cellucid']` `id`, `name`, `description`; `uns['title']` |
| `citation_text`, `citation_url` | `uns['cellucid']['citation']` |
| `source_name`, `source_url` | `uns['cellucid']['source']` |
| `embedding_defaults`, `latent_key`, `obs_keys`, `var_gene_id_column`, `vector_field_default`, `normalize_embeddings`, `centroid_min_points` | `uns['cellucid']['defaults']`, only the ones you set |
| `latent_key` (with `centroid_min_points`) | `uns['cellucid']['outlierQuantiles']`: each categorical `obs` column's outlier quantiles in that latent space |

Embeddings are stored at their own coordinates; the viewer chooses the columns
it plots and scales them to its view. `embedding_defaults` names the embedding
each view dimension shows first, by `obsm` key (its first columns) or as
`list(key = "X_pca", columns = 1:3)`.

`latent_key` names the latent space the viewer's outlier filter measures in,
such as PCA or scVI, never a 2D or 3D layout. `cellucid_prepare()` computes the
outlier quantiles of every categorical `obs` column there (each cell's
distance to its category's centre, as the share of its category at that
distance or closer) and stores them, so the filter works as soon as the file
opens. A category needs `centroid_min_points` cells (10 when not set);
`?cellucid_prepare` states the rule.

Vector fields are stored under scVelo's names and drawn over the embedding they
are named for: `vector_fields = list(velocity = list(X_umap = velocity_umap,
X_branches = velocity_branches))` stores `obsm['velocity_umap']` and
`obsm['velocity_branches']`, which the viewer lists as the one field `velocity`
and draws whenever a view shows `X_umap` or `X_branches`. Each array has one
column per column of its embedding, and the embedding's key starts with `X_`.
`cellucid_transition_drift(transition_matrix, umap, normalize_rows = TRUE)`
computes such a field from a cell-cell transition matrix (CellRank's, for
example): each cell's transition-weighted mean successor position minus its
own, ready for `vector_fields = list(T_fwd = list(X_umap = drift))`.

Cell names are the row names your inputs agree on, and gene names the `var`
row names (else the column names of `gene_expression`). Repeated names are made
unique the way anndata's `var_names_make_unique()` does it -- the second
`MATR3` becomes `MATR3-1` -- with a message saying what changed.

## Using Seurat

Seurat stores expression as **genes x cells**, and `cellucid_prepare()` expects
**cells x genes**, so transpose before passing. The function checks the
dimensions but never guesses the orientation.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
seu <- your_seurat_object

expr_genes_by_cells <- Seurat::GetAssayData(seu, layer = "data")
# The shared-nearest-neighbour graph links each cell to itself; the stored
# graph has a zero diagonal.
graph <- seu@graphs[["RNA_snn"]]
Matrix::diag(graph) <- 0

cellucid_prepare(
  out_path = "seurat.zarr",
  format = "zarr",
  embeddings = list(
    X_umap = Seurat::Embeddings(seu, "umap"),
    X_pca = Seurat::Embeddings(seu, "pca")
  ),
  dataset_id = "seurat-dataset",
  dataset_name = "Seurat dataset",
  obs = seu[[]],
  gene_expression = Matrix::t(expr_genes_by_cells),
  connectivities = graph,
  embedding_defaults = c("2d" = "X_umap"),
  latent_key = "X_pca"
)
```

## Using SingleCellExperiment

SingleCellExperiment assays are also **genes x cells**, so transpose them too.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
sce <- your_sce_object

cellucid_prepare(
  out_path = "sce.zarr",
  format = "zarr",
  embeddings = list(
    X_umap = SingleCellExperiment::reducedDim(sce, "UMAP"),
    X_pca = SingleCellExperiment::reducedDim(sce, "PCA")
  ),
  dataset_id = "sce-dataset",
  dataset_name = "SingleCellExperiment dataset",
  obs = as.data.frame(SummarizedExperiment::colData(sce)),
  var = as.data.frame(SummarizedExperiment::rowData(sce)),
  gene_expression = Matrix::t(SummarizedExperiment::assay(sce, "logcounts")),
  embedding_defaults = c("2d" = "X_umap"),
  latent_key = "X_pca"
)
```

## One file instead of a folder

`format = "zarr.zip"` writes the same store as one `.zarr.zip` file: the
format for everywhere but GitHub -- single-file hosts (a Zenodo record, a
Figshare or Hugging Face file, a bucket URL, a lab server), local files,
`cellucid serve` and Jupyter. A `.zarr` folder is the format for GitHub, which
refuses files over 100 MB and answers many small files at once over HTTP/2.
The archive's entries are stored uncompressed (each chunk is compressed
already), so the web app reads any part of it with one range request, and its
metadata comes last, so it opens with one read of the archive's end.

```{r}
archive <- cellucid_prepare(
  out_path = file.path(tempdir(), "vignette.zarr.zip"),
  format = "zarr.zip",
  embeddings = list(X_umap = umap),
  dataset_id = "vignette",
  dataset_name = "Vignette dataset",
  force = TRUE
)
file.size(archive)
```
